issue.title: chore(reposts): polish residual repost interaction paths (#4203)
issue.body:
Refs #4203 — third execution item ("residual polish") under the weekly reposts coordination parent. Owner-facing visibility (#4173) shipped via PR #4172; cold-start hardening (#3522, #3533, #3534) is in place and #3523 is deferred. This PR closes the residual-polish bucket.

## Summary

Two thematically related fixes on the repost interaction paths:

- **Observability symmetry.** `VideoInteractionsBloc._publishLike` wraps its generic catch with `Reportable(e, context: '_publishLike')` so the `DivineBlocObserver` forwards the failure to Crashlytics. `_publishRepost` used a bare `addError(e, st)` — repost publish failures were silently dropped at the dashboard. This PR wraps it with `Reportable` to mirror the like path, and lifts the two `context:` identifiers into a `VideoInteractionsReportableSites` constants class per `.claude/rules/error_handling.md` (2+ sites graduate to a per-feature constants class).

- **Reposters-fetch unification.** The metadata sheet's "Reposted by" chips used the legacy `VideoEventService.getRepostersForVideo`, which only queries Kind 16 with the `e` tag, doesn't filter Kind 5 deletions, and doesn't merge across the `a` tag. The engagement-list screen shipped in PR #4172 uses the canonical `RepostsRepository.fetchEventReposters`, which queries Kind 6 + 16, filters deletions per author, and merges `e` + `a` tags for addressable events. This PR points the cubit at the canonical method so both surfaces show the same reposter set, and removes the legacy service method (the cubit was its only production caller).

## Files changed

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/blocs/video_interactions/reportable_sites.dart` | New `VideoInteractionsReportableSites` constants class. |
| `lib/blocs/video_interactions/video_interactions_bloc.dart` | Wrap `_publishRepost` catch with `Reportable`; both sites use the constants. |
| `lib/widgets/video_feed_item/metadata/video_reposters_cubit.dart` | DI swap (`VideoEventService` → `RepostsRepository`); accepts optional `addressableId`. |
| `lib/widgets/video_feed_item/metadata/metadata_expanded_sheet.dart` | Reads `repostsRepositoryProvider` and threads `video.addressableId` to the cubit. |
| `lib/services/video_event_service.dart` | Delete `getRepostersForVideo` (only production caller migrated). |
| `test/blocs/video_interactions/video_interactions_bloc_test.dart` | Mirror the like-side `Reportable<Object>` assertion on the repost failure path. |
| `test/widgets/video_feed_item/metadata/video_reposters_cubit_test.dart` | Retarget mocks to `RepostsRepository`; preserve the `#3734` emit-after-close regression tests; add an addressable-id pass-through assertion. |
| `test/widgets/video_feed_item/actions/more_action_button_test.dart`, `test/widgets/video_feed_item/video_overlay_actions_description_test.dart`, `test/screens/feed/feed_video_overlay_test.dart` | Swap the `getRepostersForVideo` mocks for `fetchEventReposters` mocks on `repostsRepositoryProvider`. |
| `test/services/video_event_service_reposters_test.dart` | Deleted along with the underlying method. |

## Out of scope

- Migrating `metadata_expanded_sheet.dart` from `ProviderScope.containerOf` to `ConsumerWidget` + `ValueKey` per the state_management.md Riverpod → BlocProvider bridging rule. The sheet is a transient modal that dies on dismiss, so the stale-capture failure mode the rule defends against doesn't apply here. Filed as a separate consideration if a future change makes the sheet long-lived.
- `ProfileRepostedVideosBloc` `addError` consistency (Round 1 Candidate C). Its failure paths are sync/network errors that the error_handling.md matrix says should stay out of Crashlytics; the bloc's current bare-log behavior is matrix-correct.
- Cross-device count drift and double-tap UX known limitations from PR #3430.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean
- `flutter test test/blocs/video_interactions/video_interactions_bloc_test.dart` — 53/53 pass
- `flutter test test/widgets/video_feed_item/metadata/video_reposters_cubit_test.dart` — all pass (including both #3734 regression tests)
- `flutter test test/widgets/video_feed_item/actions/more_action_button_test.dart test/widgets/video_feed_item/video_overlay_actions_description_test.dart test/screens/feed/feed_video_overlay_test.dart` — all pass
- `grep -rn "getRepostersForVideo" mobile/` — zero hits

## Test plan

- [ ] Tap repost on a non-own video and force the publish to fail (airplane mode or relay block). Crashlytics should now receive a `_publishRepost` breadcrumb (was silent before).
- [ ] Open the metadata sheet on a video whose engagement-list screen shows reposters. The "Reposted by" chips should match — same set, same order, deletion-filtered.
- [ ] Open the metadata sheet on an addressable video (Kind 34236) where some reposters tagged via `a` rather than `e`. Chips now include the `a`-tagged reposters (previously missing).

comment.body: Fixed. SharedPreferences I/O was moved out of `_LibraryScreenState` entirely. `ClipsLibraryBloc` now receives a `SharedPreferences` instance via constructor injection — provided by `sharedPreferencesProvider` in the `BlocProvider` factory in `library_screen.dart`. The bloc reads the persisted sort on `ClipsLibraryLoadRequested` and writes it on `ClipsLibrarySortChanged`. The screen no longer touches prefs directly.

Fixed. The `sort.name` round-trip is gone. `ClipSort` now has an explicit `fromString` factory that maps a stable set of persisted string keys (`'newestCreation'`, `'oldestCreation'`, etc.) to enum values and falls back to the default on any unrecognised input. Enum renames can no longer silently corrupt stored prefs.

Fixed. `_sortedClips()` was removed from `_LibraryScreenState`. Sorting is now performed inside `ClipsLibraryBloc._sortClips()` at emit time, and `ClipsLibraryState` exposes a `sortedClips` field. The widget reads `state.sortedClips` directly without any derivation logic.

Fixed. `_isLibrarySelectionMode` and `_didAutoOpenSelectionMode` were removed from `_LibraryScreenState`. Both are now fields of `ClipsLibraryState`, toggled via `ClipsLibrarySelectionModeChanged` and `ClipsLibrarySelectionModeExited` events. The screen is now purely rendering and dispatching.

Fixed. The `addPostFrameCallback` inside `BlocBuilder` is gone. Tab-change/exit-selection behaviour is now handled by a `BlocListener` that reacts to `isLibrarySelectionMode` transitions and dispatches `ClipsLibrarySelectionModeExited` when the user leaves the Clips tab. The build path stays pure.

issue.title: feat(auth): add under-16 family guidance flow
issue.body:
Closes #3532

## Summary
This PR adds the client-side under-16 family guidance flow and the restricted-account review surfaces that route affected users into it.

## What Changed
- adds a welcome-screen entry point for under-16 family guidance
- adds the `/account-review` route family for welcome and moderation entry points
- adds a fail-closed checking route while authenticated moderation status is loading
- hard-gates restricted accounts to the allowed review, support, and moderation-message paths
- adds the public under-13 guidance screen and the restricted under-13 parent-support screen
- adds the 13-15 parent-consent screen and parent-contact submission screen
- sets the canonical support email to `support@divine.video`
- hosts family, kids, and age-review resources at paths on `divine.video` (e.g. `divine.video/family`) instead of separate subdomains
- fixes the support-email share fallback so the prepared body/instructions are preserved
- adds localized generic error states, Divine icon/accessibility cleanup, and focused widget/service tests

## Product Boundaries In This PR
- Under 13: parent or guardian must contact Divine support by email.
- Age 13 to 15: the parent or guardian email path is the supported handoff in this PR.
- This PR does not add private media upload, moderator tooling in other repos, or new backend review workflows.

## Main Files
- `mobile/lib/router/app_router.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_parent_consent_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_parent_contact_screen.dart`

- `mobile/lib/services/support_email_composer.dart`
- `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart`

issue.title: feat(auth): add under-16 family guidance flow
issue.body:
Closes #3532

## Summary
This PR adds the client-side under-16 family guidance flow and the restricted-account review surfaces that route affected users into it.

## What Changed
- adds a welcome-screen entry point for under-16 family guidance
- adds the `/account-review` route family for welcome and moderation entry points
- adds a fail-closed checking route while authenticated moderation status is loading
- hard-gates restricted accounts to the allowed review, support, and moderation-message paths
- adds the public under-13 guidance screen and the restricted under-13 parent-support screen
- adds the 13-15 parent-consent screen and parent-contact submission screen
- sets the canonical support email to `support@divine.video`
- hosts family, kids, and age-review resources at paths on `divine.video` (e.g. `divine.video/family`) instead of separate subdomains
- fixes the support-email share fallback so the prepared body/instructions are preserved
- adds localized generic error states, Divine icon/accessibility cleanup, and focused widget/service tests

## Product Boundaries In This PR
- Under 13: parent or guardian must contact Divine support by email.
- Age 13 to 15: the parent or guardian email path is the supported handoff in this PR.
- This PR does not add private media upload, moderator tooling in other repos, or new backend review workflows.

## Main Files
- `mobile/lib/router/app_router.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_screen.dart`
- `mobile/lib/screens/minor_account_review_parent_consent_screen.dart`

- `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart`
- `mobile/lib/l10n/app_en.arb`

comment.body:
Minor duplication after the `lib/utils/divine_video_url.dart` extraction: this anchored variant overlaps with the new `divineVideoUrlRegex`. The anchor (`^`) difference only matters if a preview line could look like `"prefix https://divine.video/video/..."`, which is not a shape `VideoSharingService` produces — `_previewPayload` splits/trims by newline first, so each line is already isolated.

If you keep both regexes, consider colocating this one in `lib/utils/divine_video_url.dart` (e.g. `divineVideoUrlLineRegex`) so both shapes live next to each other and future drift is harder. Non-blocking.

Edge case: `^"[^"]*"$` won't match a quoted-title line that contains inner double quotes. A video titled `Watch "Inception" trailer` would render in the share template as `"Watch "Inception" trailer"` and **fail** this regex, leaking the duplicate title line above the thumbnail.

If you want to harden it, anchor only the outer quotes — the contract is *"entire line is a quoted string"*, not *"no inner quotes"*:

```dart
final _quotedTitleRegex = RegExp(r'^".*"$');
```

Probably rare enough to defer, but worth a one-line tightening since the cost is zero.

I worry here a bit that we add a fix for the new infinite_video_feed (which is behind the experimental flag) that might not be required here. The point is that `videoSize` is usually reported very quickly, while `isFirstFrameRendered` can still take a short moment, which we would ignore here on android.

That means in a fast scrolling scenario, users could potentially see a black screen, since even the loading builder would no longer show up for a moment.

issue.title: chore: Gate Nostr side effects on session readiness
issue.body:
## Description

Users could lose push registration on cold launch because auth could be ready before Nostr could sign yet.
This change separates identity readiness from Nostr readiness and makes signer-dependent work wait for the matching ready client.
That matters because push registration, notification preferences, and blocklist sync all publish Nostr events.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3929

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Summary

Auth state now means the app knows who the user is.
It no longer means the Nostr client is ready to sign and publish.
The app now waits for an explicit ready session before running side effects that need the signer.

## What Changed

The flow now carries the ready pubkey and client together.
Work that publishes through Nostr rejects stale sessions and queues preferences until the matching session is ready.
Sign-out also runs outgoing push deregistration before signer teardown.

- Added `NostrSessionReadiness` and kept `isNostrReadyProvider` as a compatibility shim.
- Moved push registration, token refresh, preference publishing, push deregistration, and blocklist sync to ready-session or pre-teardown paths.
- Added warning-only wrappers so non-critical push publish failures do not escape async listeners.
- Added regression tests for cold launch, account switch, teardown ordering, queued preferences, and async error handling.

## Testing

I rebased onto latest `origin/main` and ran the full Flutter checks.
The analyzer found no issues, and the full test suite passed with 8,383 passing tests and 400 skipped tests.

- `git fetch https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile.git main:refs/remotes/origin/main && git rebase origin/main`
- `flutter analyze`
- `flutter test`

## Risks

The main risk is lifecycle ordering around sign-out and account switch.
The new tests cover the flows that could use a stale or placeholder Nostr client.
Identity-only listeners such as routing and Zendesk still use auth state.

issue.title: fix(ios-camera): restart audio capture session around AVAudioSession reconfigure
issue.body:
## Description


Fixes muted audio in recordings on iOS when the user interacts with another audio app (Spotify, a phone call, Siri, an alarm) before or during a recording.

## Why

iOS sends an `AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification` when another app takes the shared audio session. Before this change the plugin had no observer for that notification, so:

1. The session stayed in an interrupted (deactivated) state — no mic input — but `captureOutput(_:didOutput:from:)` kept running and appended silent AAC buffers to the asset writer, producing a video with a flat-line audio track.
2. After the interruption ended, the audio capture session was never restarted, so subsequent recordings were also muted until the app was relaunched.

## Manual test plan

1. Start a recording.
2. Trigger an interruption (receive a phone call, start Spotify, or
   ask Siri a question) and then dismiss it.
3. Stop the recording — verify audio is present for the portion before
   the interruption.
4. Start a new recording immediately after the interruption — verify
   audio is present throughout.
5. Repeat with Bluetooth headset connected.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3881 Closes #4171

+    /// `.shouldResume` we attempt to reactivate the session and restart the

+    /// current one) gets sound back.

+        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(

+            name: AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification,

+            let type = AVAudioSession.InterruptionType(rawValue: typeValue)
+        else { return }

+        switch type {

+            // accessor so cross-queue reads from `videoOutputQueue`

+            self.audioInterrupted = true
+            print("[DivineCameraController] AVAudioSession interruption began")

+            }()

+            // Always try to recover — even when shouldResume is false the
+            // user can still press record again and we want a working session.
+            // attachAudioToSessionIfNeeded() must run on sessionQueue (it

+            sessionQueue.async { [weak self] in

comment.body: Good catch — fixed in 03befb2dd. `audioInterrupted` is now only cleared when `attachAudioToSessionIfNeeded()` returns `true`; on failure the flag stays set so `captureOutput` keeps skipping audio appends instead of resuming writes from a still-broken session.

issue.title: feat(feed): show new divine videos in Explore Popular
issue.body:
## Summary
- Route Explore Popular through `/api/leaderboard/videos?exclude_platform=vine` so the default Popular feed promotes new divine-created videos instead of classic Vine archive imports.
- Preserve server leaderboard order, offset pagination, and defensive client-side Vine filtering.
- Fail the Explore Popular native leaderboard path without falling back to the legacy classics-heavy Popular feed.
- Refresh the Popular hashtag overlay from current `api.divine.video` hashtag data instead of the stale bundled archive-heavy list.

issue.title: fix(feed): hide Android loading overlay when first-frame callback stalls
issue.body:
## Summary
- add an Android-only feed fallback that drops the loading thumbnail once the player is ready or playing with known dimensions, even if the first-frame callback never arrives
- keep the change scoped to InfiniteVideoFeed so editor, preview, and other non-feed player flows are unchanged
- add a regression test for the Android fallback path while preserving the existing non-Android first-frame loading behavior

Closes #4301

## Verification
- flutter test test/src/widgets/infinite_video_feed_test.dart
- flutter analyze

comment.body:
## Review feedback

Thanks for keeping this scoped to `InfiniteVideoFeed` and adding a regression test for the Android first-frame callback stall. The shape is good, and CI is green, but I think one part of the fallback is too broad.

### Blocking concern

`mobile/packages/infinite_video_feed/lib/src/widgets/infinite_video_feed.dart:1183-1185`

The fallback currently hides the loading layer on Android when the controller is either `playing` **or merely `ready`**:

```dart
final allowAndroidFallback =
    _targetPlatform == TargetPlatform.android &&
    (state.isPlaying || state.status.isReady);
```

That can affect preloaded/inactive feed items. Neighboring controllers can be initialized and `ready` before they are the active playing page. If the loading thumbnail is removed for an inactive ready controller that has not rendered a first frame, swiping toward that page can reveal a blank/native surface instead of the thumbnail.

This also conflicts with the player state contract in `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/lib/src/video_player_state.dart:101-106`, which explicitly says to use `isFirstFrameRendered`, not `PlaybackStatus.ready`, to hide placeholders.

I’d scope the fallback to the active page or to actual playback only. For example, pass `isActive: index == _currentIndex` into `_shouldShowLoadingLayer`, and allow `status.isReady` only when active, or simplify to Android + `state.isPlaying`.

### Test coverage gap

`mobile/packages/infinite_video_feed/test/src/widgets/infinite_video_feed_test.dart:484-502`

The new Android regression test uses a single-video feed, so it only covers the active item path. It does not catch the inactive/preloaded ready-controller case above.

Please add a two-video Android test where the next/previous controller is ready with dimensions but not playing and confirm the loading layer remains until the page becomes active or the player is actually playing.

issue.title: feat(inbox): redesign conversation screen and inbox previews
issue.body:
Closes #4287 ## Description End-to-end redesign of the DM screens (Messages tab and a single conversation). Touches the top "Contacts" carousel, the conversation list rows, the conversation header, the messages surface card, the message bubbles, the shared-video-in-DM card, the long-press action menus, and the report flow. Also fixes an inbox correctness bug (last-message preview was reading a denormalized column that could go stale), expands the app-bar icon button tap target to a true 48×48, unifies the DM-message and video report flows on one bottom sheet, and migrates eight DM-screen hardcoded English strings to \`context.l10n\`. ### A note on scope The supporting changes outside \`lib/screens/inbox\` might look unrelated to the DM-screen scope at first glance. While polishing the conversation header and the in-bubble shared-video card, I needed two cross-surface guarantees to also hold — those fixes only made sense applied consistently across every surface they touch, otherwise the same data would render differently on the conversation screen versus everywhere else. - \`lib/widgets/profile/profile_header_widget.dart\` — only a rename: \`_truncateNpubForDisplay\` (the helper that produces \`npub1xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx…\` for the profile screen subtitle) is now public so the conversation header can fall back to the same identifier shape when the participant has no NIP-05. Two surfaces, one helper. Letting the conversation header invent its own truncation would have meant the same user showed two different secondary identifiers depending on which screen you opened. - \`lib/widgets/report_content_dialog.dart\` — generalized to take either a video or an \`(eventId, authorPubkey)\` pair. The bottom sheet that opens from the home-feed video overlay's Report action and the bottom sheet that opens from a DM bubble's long-press > Report are now the same widget with the same UX (reason cards, "Other"-expands-to-details, in-sheet confirmation). The legacy \`ReportMessageDialog\` AlertDialog is gone. - \`packages/divine_ui/lib/src/app_bar/divine_app_bar_icon_button.dart\` — fixes a 40×40 tap target that should always have been 48×48 (the 4 px halo around the visible pill was previously decorative, not tappable). Caught while reviewing the conversation header; the fix applies everywhere \`DiVineAppBarIconButton\` is used. - \`packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart\` — the inbox preview was reading the conversations table's denormalized \`lastMessageContent\` / \`lastMessageTimestamp\`, which can go stale when an older gift wrap arrives after a newer one during backfill. Reworked the read pipeline to overlay the actual latest message from \`direct_messages\` on every emit; messages-table is the source of truth. In an ideal world these would be separate PRs. Given the redesign was already cross-cutting and the supporting changes are read-only or rename-level, they're shipped together — reviewers can take each section below as its own logical PR. The four supporting items have their own test coverage (\`dm_repository_test\` adds two overlay tests, the report-flow refactor reuses the existing \`report_content_dialog_test\` suite, the app-bar tap-target stays green against the existing \`divine_app_bar_icon_button_test\`). ## Screenshots ### Inbox — Contacts row (FollowingBar)
Main This branch
Inbox > Messages tab, top of the screen — Contacts carousel with names truncated to one line ("Sensitive...", "Clever Tyra...") Same row — names wrap to two lines ("Sensitive Rabbit 68", "Clever Tyrannosauru..."). Tighter 8 px left inset; no extra bottom padding.
### Inbox — conversation list rows (ConversationTile)
Main This branch
Inbox > Messages tab, scroll list — preview text shows the FIRST message of each conversation (the historic backfill stale value); avatar centered with column; shared-video DM previews show the raw URL alongside the title. Same conversations — preview shows the LATEST message (read from direct_messages, not the denormalized column); avatar top-anchored to the name's first line; shared-video DM previews show a small camera icon + title, URL stripped.
### Inbox — long-press actions sheet on a conversation row
Main This branch
Long-press any conversation row — actions sheet slides up but stops above the bottom nav bar, nav bar still visible. Same gesture — sheet covers the bottom nav bar entirely (routed through the root Navigator), matching the home-feed Comments / Report sheets.
### Conversation — header
Main This branch

issue.body:
Summary:
The Explore Popular native-only path currently relies on /api/leaderboard/videos?exclude_platform=vine plus a repository-side defensive Vine filter because /api/v2/videos?sort=popular&exclude_platform=vine does not reliably honor the exclusion.

Why this exists:
- PR #4304 needs native-only Popular now.
- The intended v2 listing path is not honoring exclude_platform=vine consistently.
- Offset pagination must remain aligned to raw leaderboard rows even when some rows are filtered client-side.

Removal criteria:
- Funnelcake fixes /api/v2/videos?sort=popular&exclude_platform=vine so classic Vine rows are excluded server-side.
- Mobile can switch Explore Popular off the leaderboard workaround and delete the repository-side defensive filter and TODOs.

- PR #4304
